verifiedProduct.failureFirstObservation: Failure-first tests proved the hidden snapshot cap: runtime-native snapshot options received max=400 instead of undefined and a synthetic page with 450 qualifying elements returned 400; the other 82 unit tests passed.
verifiedProduct.change: Generic Playwright-backed and runtime-native Lightpanda snapshots no longer impose Ferrum's implicit 400-element default ceiling. StepEngine passes no limit unless a caller explicitly supplies a positive max.

challengePass.reason: Native desktop adapters and compact-state ideas require new real-platform or identical-workload experiments. Shipping one now would be speculative; the snapshot-cap fix is the only material change that crossed the proof gate.

nextExperiments: Benchmark snapshot-scoped ref epochs plus optional progressive skeleton/delta as derived output while retaining the complete uncapped raw snapshot; measure bytes, tool calls, stale-target failures and task success.
Prototype a temporary Cua Driver/Sandbox native-app adapter on a deterministic real desktop fixture when a qualifying host exists; compare lifecycle, evidence and focus/cursor side effects.
Adapt a compact DeskCraft/PPT-Eval/WindowsWorld-style task subset with deterministic intermediate and final-artifact checks.
Evaluate MacAgentBench only on real qualifying macOS infrastructure.
guardrails: Complete browser snapshots remain default: no hidden count cap, viewport-only processing, culling, deferred off-screen omission, fidelity reduction or stale cache.
Explicit positive snapshot max is caller opt-in and is never injected by StepEngine.
Compact skeleton/delta ideas remain derived views while complete raw evidence stays available.
New native/visual adapters remain additive until real-runtime parity and measurable benefit are proven per platform.
Synthetic benchmarks never replace Linux, Windows browser/MV3, packaged desktop, Lightpanda, Selenium Grid or Android/Appium gates.
